MQ-6 SCOPE ADDITION (from MQ-3 Option-A re-sequencing, 2026-06-02). Because MQ-3 made test-ruleset-design-invariants.sh transition-tolerant (dual-mode) instead of hard-flipping it, the live-state-coupled deletions move here and MUST execute ATOMICALLY in lockstep with the live re-provision (provision-ruleset.sh --enable-merge-queue):
  1. Provision the merge_queue rule onto the live MAIN ruleset (flips the invariant test's discriminator to MQ mode automatically).
  2. Remove 'check-staged-head' from .github/required-checks.txt AND re-provision the live MAIN ruleset so check-staged-head is no longer a required context (else PRs wedge on a context that no longer reports).
  3. Delete .github/workflows/check-staged-head.yml.
  4. Delete the live staged-* sub-PR ruleset (16961402 'DSO Sub-PR Review Enforcement') — coordinate with the MQ-4 STORY_PR_BASE decision (sub-PRs move to session branch); if review-sub-pr enforcement is retained on session branches, REPURPOSE rather than delete, and extend the invariant test MQ-branch with the final sub-PR assertion.
  5. Delete the now-dead TWO-TIER assertion branch (I1-I6) from test-ruleset-design-invariants.sh — realizes the ADR's 'smaller drift surface' win. Keep the MQ branch (M1/M2/I7).
ORDERING SAFETY: the dual-mode test tolerates BOTH states, so the order of effects within MQ-6 has slack (a mid-cutover hiccup won't instantly red-wedge ruleset-design-invariants). Sequence the merge_group-trigger / merge-pipeline-checks merge_group arm (MQ-4/step-2) BEFORE enabling the queue or entries silently reject. Related: G2 — sprint/check-ruleset-preflight.sh (MQ-5) must also tolerate/flip to the MQ model in the same window or sprint Phase A wedges.
